symbolic_theorem_target.name: SHORT_PARENT_BAD_SECTOR_CONTAINMENT
symbolic_theorem_target.domain: canonical CNF with maximum parent clause width <= 4
symbolic_theorem_target.statement: For a pivot v, every retained non-tautological cross-polarity resolvent of width > 4 has both parent clauses of width >= 3. Equivalently BAD(v) is a subset of P_ge3(v) x N_ge3(v).
proof_kernel: A pivot parent of width 2 leaves a residual of size at most 1 after removing v or -v.
Every opposite parent in W4 leaves a residual of size at most 3.
Therefore if either parent has width <= 2, the resolvent union has size at most 1+3=4.
Hence any retained resolvent of width > 4 requires both parents to have width >= 3.
symbolic_theorem_target.stronger_width6_corollary: A retained width-6 resolvent in W4 can arise only from a width-4 x width-4 parent pair with disjoint residuals.

required_checks: Every actual retained bad pair on the audited corpus obeys the short-parent bad-sector containment theorem.
Every width>4 clause in the exact DP transformed formula is traceable to an independently enumerated long-long bad resolvent.
The exact R50C 52-root trajectory is replayed without heuristic or random authority.
Exactly 12 rank1-fail/rank2-rescue states are recovered before synthesis is accepted.
Frozen transfer candidates are reported whether supported or falsified; none may be rewritten after execution.
falsifiers: Any retained width>4 cross resolvent with a width-2 parent falsifies SHORT_PARENT_BAD_SECTOR_CONTAINMENT.
Any width>4 exact-DP clause not derivable from an independently enumerated long-long bad resolvent is an integrity failure.
Any mismatch with R50C top2 outcome replay is an integrity failure.
Any frozen transfer candidate may be explicitly falsified by one of the 12 rescue states.
